# fluss-go v0.1.0-beta.4

This prerelease hardens data-path behavior after v0.1.0-beta.3 and expands
compatible reads across Apache Fluss 0.9.1 schema versions.

## Highlights

- Resolves historical schema IDs for point and prefix lookups, current-state
  batches, and row and Arrow log batches.
- Maps compatible schema changes by stable field ID, including renames,
  dropped columns, and newly nullable columns.
- Runs log and KV requests for distinct buckets concurrently while preserving
  strict per-bucket order and bounded writer memory.
- Bounds both server operations and client-side writer network calls.
- Adds aggregate byte and file-count limits to remote log and snapshot reads
  and retries only explicitly transient failures.
- Makes transport cancellation, request completion, writer shutdown, and
  filesystem-token receiver shutdown deterministic.
- Preserves a final non-empty snapshot batch returned together with `io.EOF`.
- Makes fuzz smoke tests deterministic and removes false error lines from
  successful GitHub Actions coverage logs.

## Upgrade notes

- The default log and KV writer concurrency is four requests across distinct
  buckets. Use `WithLogConcurrency(1)` or `WithKVConcurrency(1)` when an
  application requires the previous single-request scheduling behavior.
- `RemoteFileReadConfig` now defaults to at most 512 MiB and 4096 files per
  remote-log or snapshot operation. Set explicit lower limits to match the
  application's memory budget.
- After altering a table, open the table again and construct new readers with
  the refreshed `fgo.Table`. Existing readers retain the result schema they
  were created with.
- Snapshot consumers must process rows in a result even when `Done` is true;
  the final rows and completion marker may arrive together.

See the [full changelog](../../CHANGELOG.md), the
[schema-evolution guide](../../docs/schema-evolution.md), and the
[data-operations guide](../../docs/data-operations.md).

This is a pre-v1 release. Pin the version and review the changelog before
upgrading.
